Nothing lands on `main` until it is green again (only a branch opened to fix it does), no other review of it starts, and branches already approved go back to review. The red tip is first in the review queue (`red-main-60bf819c3342`); a reviewer looks for what in `main`'s history broke it. With the `queue` tool you can read both queues and the gate's evidence (`action: "status"`), gate the tip again once the cause is gone — a flake, the machine, a gate fixed outside the target (`"regate"`), withdraw a row that no longer means anything (`"withdraw"`), and restart a parked one (`"restart"`). If the gate is wrong for this branch — it names another branch's artifact, or the project lands on another branch — say so: `"propose_target"` puts the `[queue] target` line of the project's `leticode.toml` to the operator, whose decision it is.
